rationale: ROUND 2 (RESUBMIT_CORR=75091072-9d65-433e-8a30-84719dc3f30f). Round 1 (run ae2a88a7) returned REVISE on a gating HIGH objection from reuse_agent, and the objection is correct: RFC_029 Phase 1 (commits 927e12bd9 + 1806371ef, now LIVE in chassis v1.0.1303 — binary stamped 5e075a6f9, probed 2026-08-16 with a must-be-absent control) made the whole-tree search deterministic and added two WARNs ('aggressive search: conflicting candidates', 'aggressive search: explicit single-segment mapping bypassed') as the instrument for a 48h+ observation window that gates Phase 2 (RFC_029 §9 D2: conflicts flip to refusal only on zero conflict WARNs, or every observed pair explicitly mapped). Those WARNs were plain zap log lines; chassis pod log retention is ~90 seconds (CTS-059), so the window could not be read after the fact. The platform's remedy already exists — agent_error_log via platform/orchestration/agenterrors (RFC_012's ONE writer) — and reuse_agent named it. THIS REVISION persists EVERY occurrence of both WARNs to agent_error_log (no dedup: frequency is the population §9's disconfirmation clause needs), keeps the log lines for live tailing, and changes NOTHING about resolution. MECHANISM: findFieldRecursive/ExtractActionInputs carry no *sql.DB or ctx and have ~115 call sites, so instead of threading a handle, datahelpers gains a package-level registered sink — SetResolverFindingRecorder(func(ResolverFinding)) — nil by default (= log-only = the previous build, the default-OFF shape of the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling). The chassis registers one in agentbase.initializeComponents immediately after the pool is created (the one place the DB and pod identity both exist), as a thin wrapper over orchestration.LogAgentError → agenterrors.Write, synchronous under a detached 5s timeout exactly like the sibling recorders in that file (recordRejectedIncomingMessage, recordFailedProcessing). Row shape: error_code RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES / RESOLVER_MAPPING_BYPASSED, severity 'warning', action 'input-resolver' (deliberately not a registered action name), error_message = the WARN text verbatim, context = the WARN's structured fields + identity_scope. KNOWN LIMIT stated on every row: orchestration_id/step_name are empty by design (not reachable from the resolver); attribution is pod_name + agent_type. A recorder panic is recovered inside datahelpers so the instrument can never change the resolver's answer. THE OTHER FIVE SEATS' OBJECTIONS ARE ANSWERED WITHOUT CODE and the evidence is IN THE DB this time (doc_notes decision/RFC_029 = the ruling's key lines + what shipped + the codes + the window query; doc_notes decision/council-submission-75091072 = this round's checks with the queries that produced them): editquality — the two 'missing D4' items (extractSingleField arm renames; migration 402's dated correction) SHIPPED in 1806371ef, the round-1 plan simply failed to list them; guardian — 'the winner changes now' is §9 D2's explicit owner-delegated choice (stable shallowest-first over a coin flip; instrument first, refuse second); tooling_provenance — ledger checked (schema_migrations keys on FILENAME: 417_brief_fidelity… applied by another lane, 417_image_build_handler…HOLD unclaimed, no collision) and the doc_notes rows above are written; debug_historian — measured: image-build-handler has exactly 1 active row (two-active-rows trap N/A) and snapshot_agent(text,text) writes agent_definitions_backup (pg_get_functiondef), both now in 417's header with the has-old-key rollback check, and the pod-verification recipe is the CLAUDE.md two-way /proc/1/exe probe (run today: 5e075a6f9 present, HEAD bc4cd65e7 absent); prior_art_librarian — owner rulings in markdown are invisible to seats (known gate landmine), hence the decision/RFC_029 row. WHAT WOULD DISCONFIRM THIS REVISION: (a) a second writer against agent_error_log — there is none, both paths go through agenterrors.Write; (b) the recorder changing a resolved value — tests pin same value + same WARN with and without a recorder and under a panicking one; (c) the row population diverging from the WARN population — tests pin one finding per WARN and zero for the agreeing/never-resolvable controls, mutation-proven at both call sites.

plan.summary: The RFC_029 Phase 1 observation instrument (two WARNs) was log-only on a platform with ~90s pod log retention, so its 48h+ window was unreadable after the fact — the round-1 gating objection. This revision persists every occurrence of both WARNs to agent_error_log through the ONE writer (agenterrors.Write via orchestration.LogAgentError), via a nil-by-default registered sink in datahelpers that the chassis installs at startup where the pool and pod identity live. Resolution behaviour is unchanged; the log lines stay; per-run identity is stated as pod-level on every row. Round-1's five secondary objections are answered by measurements now written into migration 417's header and into two doc_notes rows readable by seats. All Go; inert until the next chassis roll; the window's clock starts at that roll. (Migration 417's header carries the measured pre-apply checks — comment-only, so it is evidence here, not an edit.)

Thin wrapper over the ONE writer (orchestration.LogAgentError → agenterrors.Write), synchronous under a detached 5s timeout exactly like recordRejectedIncomingMessage/recordFailedProcessing in the same file — no second writer, no fork. agentbase already imports orchestration (which imports datahelpers), so the new import is cycle-free.

Pins the contract at the resolver on a FAKE recorder (never a mocked INSERT — that is agenterrors' contract): one conflict → exactly one finding (code, field, all 3 candidate paths, winner) and a second conflict → a second; one bypass → exactly one; agreeing / never-resolvable controls → zero (row population == WARN population); no recorder → same value + same WARN (default-OFF control); a panicking recorder cannot change the answer. plan.risks: (1) A synchronous DB write inside the resolver: bounded by a 5s timeout and reached only on the conflict/bypass branches, which are off the happy path; if the bypass population turns out large the cost is one small INSERT per affected step, and that population size is exactly what the window measures. Reviewer check: no goroutine, no queue — a lost row is the writer's own WARN, never a silent drop. (2) Pod-level attribution only — orchestration_id/step_name empty by design; a reader could mistake that for a defect, so every row's context carries identity_scope and the RUNBOOK/RFC say so. (3) Zero rows after the roll has two readings (no conflicts vs the revised build has not rolled) — disambiguate with the binary probe + merge-base, per SERVICE. (4) Non-chassis binaries that use datahelpers without agentbase stay log-only (nil recorder) — stated, not hidden; the chassis is where the resolver runs for orchestration steps. (5) Migration 417 remains HELD; its binary precondition is now met but applying it is a separate hand step with the header's checks.
